a: Unit tests isolate one piece; integration tests cover real boundaries.
End-to-end tests drive the product like a user through a critical path.
Many unit tests, fewer integration tests, few e2e tests.
Run cheapest tests first so failures show up quickly.
Snapshots drift; review updates instead of blindly accepting.
Tests must not depend on each other or shared mutable state.
Mock external HTTP in unit tests; use recorded fixtures for contract tests.
